submission.justification: CONDITIONAL RECOMMENDATION. Do not order crystals until K2's intrinsic background has been measured or certified. On resolution alone, Crystal-K2 at about 5 cm is clearly the best choice. In simulation it gave 2.86% FWHM at 662 keV, compared with 4.55% for K1 and 8.67% for K3. Best values found for the other thicknesses tested: K1 4.82% at 3 cm, K3 8.90% at 3 cm. K2 scan: 3.35% (2 cm), 2.92% (3 cm), 2.95% (4.5 cm), 2.86% (5 cm), 2.89% (6 cm), 3.19% (8 cm), 4.31% (10 cm). This means the 4.5–6 cm range is flat and resolution gets worse above about 6 cm. These results match the 2025 summary. However, I could not check the hard constraint on intrinsic background (no more than 0.5 counts/kg/day, 100–3000 keV). None of the project documents give intrinsic-background figures for any candidate, and the simulation tool only reports resolution. I also have one specific concern. A 'high light yield, fast decay' crystal like K2 is typical of lanthanum-halide-type scintillators. These can carry intrinsic radioactivity, for example La-138 and Ac-227 chain contamination, far above 0.5 counts/kg/day. That would rule them out for a low-background screening facility. I am inferring this only from the description; I have not confirmed it. Before procurement (planned for Q2), the collaboration should get vendor radiopurity certificates or a low-background screening measurement for K2. If K2 fails the budget, choose the next-best candidate that passes: K1, about 3–5 cm, at about 4.6–4.8% FWHM. If that also fails, choose K3.
